If a household lacks elderly members over 60 years of age, a middle-aged man aged 40 years or older may carry out bamboo planting [2]. This rule applies when the strict requirement for an oldest male member cannot be met due to the absence of individuals over 60 in the house [1]. The belief that only very old men should plant bamboo is deeply rooted among older households but less so among younger, better-educated families [1]. Consequently, middle-aged household heads or members aged 40 years and above are permitted to perform this task in the absence of older relatives [2].
